specification.problem: Analyze search for a marked vertex on the complete graph of N vertices by a lackadaisical quantum walk, where each vertex has l self-loops. Compare the discrete-time phase-flip coin, the SKW (2003) coin, and the continuous-time walk, and determine how success probability and runtime depend on l.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Abstract-level reconstruction of the single-marked-vertex complete-graph search. Only the qualitative effects of l are stated in the abstract. Explicit coin operators, the walk Hamiltonian, optimal l and runtimes, and the multiple-marked-vertex generalization are not given and are left unreconstructed.

symbols.meaning: number of vertices of the complete graph
number of self-loops attached to each vertex
success probability of finding the marked vertex

equations.label: Phase-flip coin success with one self-loop
equations.description: For the phase flip coin, adding one self-loop to each vertex raises the success probability from 1/2 to 1.
equations.abstract_quote: adding a self-loop to each vertex boosts the success probability from $1/2$ to $1$

equations.label: Quantum speedup conditions
equations.description: The scaling of l below which the walk is faster than classical search: l less than N for the phase flip coin and less than N^2 for the SKW coin.
equations.abstract_quote: the first is faster than classical when $l$ scales less than $N$, while the second requires that $l$ scale less than $N^{2}$
equations.justification: Paraphrases the abstract's scaling statements as asymptotic conditions.

registers.name: position
registers.role: walker location; marked vertex is one basis state

registers.name: coin
registers.role: edge and self-loop directions; N-1 edges to other vertices plus l self-loops

specification.initial_state: Assumed: uniform superposition over all vertices and all coin directions (including self-loops). Not specified in the abstract; for the lackadaisical walk the weighting of self-loop components may differ.

steps.description: Prepare the assumed initial state on the position and coin registers.

Repeat for discrete-time walks: apply an oracle coin at the marked vertex (phase flip coin or SKW coin) and other vertices use a Grover diffusion coin over N-1+l directions; then apply the shift, which swaps along edges and leaves self-loop components in place. Uses l=1 for the phase flip coin to reach p=1.
For continuous-time walk, evolve under a walk Hamiltonian with an oracle term; per the abstract, self-loops make no difference to the outcome. The Hamiltonian is not given.

specification.measurement: Assumed: after the chosen number of walk steps (or evolution time), measure the position register in the vertex basis and accept the outcome if it equals the marked vertex; the coin register is ignored/traced out. Success probability p is the probability of obtaining the marked vertex.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Assumed: check whether the measured vertex is the marked one (one oracle query); if not, repeat the walk and measurement. Expected repetitions are about 1/p. The optimal stopping time is not given in the abstract.
assumptions: Register sizes and initial state are assumed finite instances, not taken from the abstract.
Coin register has N-1+l directions per vertex.
Measurement is a standard position-basis measurement with repetition; not stated in the abstract.
Measurement is a position-basis measurement with classical repetition, assumed.
